producer_report.summary: Merge refusals logged while required checks were pending no longer fire D87's hard signal. Root cause: landing already treated a rule-violation refusal followed by pending checks as a wait. But the client had logged it as a plain host-error record, and `HostErrorSignal::matches` compared only operation, phase and status. Fix: `athena.host-error/1` has a new optional `checks_pending` field (serde default, omitted when false). Old records parse and write unchanged. `land_pr` calls a new defaulted `PrHost::note_pending_merge_refusal` in the existing "rule violation, checks Pending" branch. `GhClient` implements it with `HostErrorLog::mark_last_pending(Merge)`. `matches` skips flagged records. `D87_SIGNAL`'s name string is unchanged. A 405 or 422 with the checks settled, and any other refusal, are logged and fire as before. Tests, the D87_SIGNAL doc comment, a CHANGELOG entry and a D87 note in decisions.md are in. No file under records/ is edited and the open D87 review is not cleared. I did not run the full `cargo test`.

mistakes: My first draft of the mixed-job watcher test used an invalid record id suffix, so the first test run failed. I fixed the id and reran.
learnings: `HostError` has `deny_unknown_fields`. An older athena binary would refuse a record that carries `checks_pending`. Only records written after this change for pending refusals are affected.
Test record ids need a four-character Crockford suffix (no `l`, `i`, `o` or `u`); `RecordId::parse` refuses others.
`land_pr` holds `&dyn PrHost`, not the log, so a defaulted `PrHost` hook was the way to reach the client's log.
Only four `HostError` struct literals exist: watcher.rs (derive and test helper), transport.rs, records.rs tests. All are updated.
desires: The open review 20261031-085139-1y06 and record 20261101-174051-3t6g are absent from the snapshot, so I could not read them. The old-format test uses a hand-written JSON literal with the same fields as the 3t6g shape. The job id in it is made up.
